plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Exit remaining AI/Software leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, PLTU).
Reduce SPY to 20% to address concentration.
Hold a significant cash buffer for capital preservation.
Focus on broad index and quality names for stability.
Maintain tight stops to limit potential losses.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and concentrates on stability, aiming for low drawdowns. Risk is minimized by cutting high-beta and leveraged positions.

plan: Exit remaining leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU).
Reduce AI/Software leveraged positions (METU, MSFU, PLTU).
Trim SPY to 25% to meet concentration mandate.
Maintain a moderate cash buffer of around 10%.
Blend broad index exposure with quality tech names.
Focus on risk reduction while seeking growth.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets ~2.5% monthly return by prioritizing risk management. It reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for steady growth with controlled drawdowns. The plan balances broad market exposure with select tech holdings.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to comply with concentration limits.
Buy SPXS (inverse ETF) to hedge against market downturns.
Increase exposure to SOXL (3x semiconductor ETF) to 5%.
Increase exposure to SPAL (2x space ETF) to 5%.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer of approximately 5%.
Utilize strict stop discipline on all positions.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly return by leaning into leverage and concentration. It increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and adds hedging. Expect higher potential upside but also significantly larger drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses due to leverage decay. Strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) and leveraged AI/Software (METU, MSFU, PLTU).
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration.
Increase QQQI (income ETF) to 30% for steady distributions.
Prioritize reliable monthly income over aggressive growth.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
Focus on low drawdown and consistent income generation.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% monthly return through distributions. It shifts away from leverage and high-beta names towards income-generating ETFs like QQQI. While prioritizing stability and income, NAV can still decline in market selloffs, and distributions are not guaranteed.
